construct.constructDefinition: Teaching and learning: teacher self-positioning on digital-competence maturity statements. Preserves each competence’s A1–C2 statement and separate zero-point not-aware response; not an agreement scale, a teaching-quality measure or an observed performance test. No area/global aggregate is computed by this split unit.

population.populationNotes: Adult primary and secondary teachers able to understand the fixed English Toolkit. Initial digital split scope; age18+ is a project scope, not a source-derived validation cut-off. Source studies do not establish Chinese-language or separate-area digital equivalence. Early-years use on the current website is not borrowed as validation for this fixed primary/secondary version.

administration.timeFrame: Current professional digital practice and experience; no fixed day/week recall period.
layoutConstraints: Choose the ONE original maturity statement that best describes your current competence in each item. Six item-specific A1/A2/B1/B2/C1/C2 statements are scored1–6, and the seventh not-aware response is scored0.
Keep the original competence order and original option order; no agreement anchors, automatic reversal, simplified alternatives or shortened items.
Six separate native area units are project packaging; independent administration equivalence is not established. The ordinary-composite recipe retains all32 competences in order.
This unit reports each competence separately; no area mean, global192-point total or overall A1–C2 band is manufactured across the split tools.

Missing items remain null; 0 is a real not-aware answer, not missing data. Any unanswered competence makes this area incomplete and suppresses its interpretations; this complete-area policy is a project choice, not an inferred source missing-data algorithm.
Timing is an approximate project allocation of the official circa25-minute whole-tool estimate, not measured timing.

intendedUses.notes: Professional learning self-reflection using a fixed EU source, not a certification, teacher appraisal or observed competence test.
Separate-area digital packaging and local applicability require explicit interpretation limits; not automatic cross-language/role equivalence.

options.label: A1: I am aware that digital technologies can support and enhance teaching and learning (e.g. software programs and suites, mobile apps and tools, on-line and cloud-based resources).

A2: I have tried using digital technologies to support and/or enhance my teaching practice (e.g. software programs and suites, mobile apps and tools, online and cloud-based resources, interactive whiteboards).

B1: I use various digital technologies that can support innovative pedagogical approaches, enhancing my students' active involvement in their learning (e.g. inquiry based learning, project based learning, game based learning, peer and self assessment, e-portfolios, student coaches).
B2: I select and use digital technologies in my learning designs, so as to meet teaching and learning aims (e.g. simulations, digital games, online interactive tools, collaborative environments).

C1: Together with my students, I reflect on and (re)design the use of digital technologies to enhance teaching practices and innovative learning approaches (e.g. students as coaches, use of emerging technologies, modelling and advice, lesson-study).

C2: I initiate and promote the design and sharing of innovative teaching and learning practices with digital technologies in my school and its wider community (e.g. online workshops, learning design with the use of digital technologies, micro-teaching and co-teaching, reflective discussions on the effectiveness of the use of digital technologies).
I am not aware of this competence.
A1: I am aware that digital technologies can be used to provide and receive feedback and opportunities to reflect on teaching and learning practices (e.g. email, chat, video response).
A2: I have tried using digital technologies to provide feedback and support to students (e.g., online tutorials, chat, automated/immediate feedback, links to online Q&A).

B1: I use various digital technologies to provide students with feedback and opportunities for reflection on their learning, in real-time and /or asynchronously (e.g. chat, discussion forums, video responses, in-class polls/ voting).

B2: I select and employ digital technologies to provide opportunities for students to engage in self-assessment and peer-assessment and the design of their learning (e.g. online shared documents, recordings of learning activities, scaffolded reflection).

C1: Together with my students, I reflect on and (re)design teaching and learning, based on evidence captured through digital technologies (e.g. digital polls/surveys outcomes, recordings of learning activities, learning analytics).

C2: I initiate and promote ways in which digital technologies can be used to support feedback and reflection for teachers and students in my school and beyond (e.g. discussion forums, chat, shared documents, Frequently Asked Questions).
I am not aware of this competence.
A1: I am aware that digital technologies can be used to foster and enhance learner collaboration towards individual and collective learning (e.g. on-line collaboration, sharing learning resources).
A2: I have tried using digital technologies to support and enhance collaborative activities of students (e.g. shared documents, contributing to forums, wikis).
B1: I use various digital technologies to support and enhance students' collaborative learning, in face-to-face and/ or online settings (e.g. shared documents, forums, wikis, blogs, co-authoring).

B2: I select and employ digital technologies in my learning designs based on their features, so as to enhance and support my students' collaborative learning, in face to face and/or online settings (e.g. co-design, co-creation, peer assessment and group reflection, project building, sharing).

C1: Together with my students, I reflect on and (re)design their use of digital technologies for individual and/or collaborative learning (e.g. edit and develop content, co-create an artefact, participate in collaborative projects, virtual exchanges, use of digital tools for task and time management, communication and sharing).

C2: I initiate and promote the use of digital technologies within my school and its wider community, providing opportunities for collaboration to support individual and collective learning, in and beyond the school (e.g. using synchronous and asynchronous online environments and tools, teach meets, joint projects, co-organising online learning events, co-designing and co-creating learning material).
I am not aware of this competence.
A1: I am aware that digital technologies can be used to foster active and autonomous learning (e.g. planning, goal setting, recording progress).

A2: I have tried using digital technologies to support students in planning their own learning (e.g. planning and scheduling using digital calendars, goal setting using digital journals, recording progress).

B1: I use various digital technologies to support students plan and regulate their own learning (e.g. online learning environments, online resources repositories, collaborative tools and spaces, learning journals, e-portfolios).

B2: I select and use digital technologies in my learning designs based on their features, so as to facilitate my students' self-regulated learning skills and learner autonomy (e.g. take initiatives regarding their own learning, be creative and responsive to new learning situations, engage in self-reflections so as to plan and guide their progress).

C1: Together with my students, I reflect on and support them to (re)design their learning, through and on using digital technologies, promoting their self-regulated learning and learner autonomy (e.g. identify their needs, set their learning goals, describe their strategy for achieving these goals, implement their learning tasks, gather evidence of their learning, reflect on it and share their learning outcomes).

C2: I initiate and promote strategies and practices on how digital technologies can support self-regulated learning in my school and in the wider community (e.g. makerspaces, learning spaces with digital technologies to accommodate hands-on activities, student coaching).
I am not aware of this competence.
A1: I am aware of emerging technologies that are being used in educational settings (e.g. simulations, robotics, virtual reality, Artificial Intelligence (AI)).
A2: I have tried emerging technologies to see their relevance for my teaching and my students (e.g. virtual and augmented reality, robots, AI).

B1: I use various emerging technologies to provide my students with novel learning experiences and new kinds of learning, fostering the development of transversal skills (learning experiences involving e.g. simulating/modelling, gaming, computational thinking, creative and innovative thinking, data-driven decision making).

B2: I select and use emerging technologies in my learning designs to engage my students in novel learning opportunities, while taking into account ethical implications (e.g. immersive learning, computational thinking, addressing learner agency when interacting with AI).

C1: Together with my students, I reflect on and (re)design teaching and learning, engaging them in co-design and co-creation of applications using emerging technologies and addressing ethical implications (e.g. designing augmented reality scenarios and 3D expeditions, programming humanoid robots, addressing datafication and AI agency in decision making).

C2: I initiate and promote strategies and practices within my school and its wider community that can support colleagues and students in their use of emerging technologies to provide novel teaching and learning experiences and content, while addressing ethical implications (e.g. customise virtual worlds for learning activities, foster human agency in data-driven decision making, collaboration with technology companies).
I am not aware of this competence.

items.content: 3.1. Teaching and Learning – Teaching Designing, developing and implementing learning with the use of digital technologies to enhance learning outcomes.

3.2. Teaching and Learning - Guidance Using digital technologies in order to provide feedback and opportunities for reflection, leading to readjustment of teaching and learning practices for both teeachers and learners.
3.3. Teaching and Learning - Collaborative Learning Using digital technologies to foster and enhance learner collaboration for individual and collective learning.

3.4. Teaching and Learning - Self-regulated learning Using digital technologies to enhance students' self-regulated learning processes, fostering active and autonomous learning making students more responsible for their own learning, thereby shifting the focus from teaching to learning.
3.5. Teaching and Learning - Emerging technologies Using emerging technologies in ethical ways to explore novel learning experiences and content.

interpretations.headline: Reflecting on competence 3.1
interpretations.summary: This response records the maturity statement you selected for this specific digital competence. The statements describe awareness, exploration, use, purposeful selection, reflective support and wider initiative in item-specific ways. A higher point value indicates a later self-described position in this framework; it does not establish better teaching or better student outcomes. The separate not-aware response is a valid starting point for learning. Use a recent example and your working conditions to put the choice in context. The displayed points preserve the original statement order: 0 = not aware; 1 = A1; 2 = A2; 3 = B1; 4 = B2; 5 = C1; 6 = C2. These codes are maturity statements within this framework, not agreement levels, teacher grades or population percentiles.

guidance.text: Choose one recent example connected with this competence. What did you do, what evidence did you notice, and which conditions helped or limited it?
Choose one lesson and one learning aim. Try a small digital activity only if it helps that aim, then look at a sample of students’ work.
You can start with a small, supported trial. Technical resources, time and local policies affect what is feasible.

limitations: Fixed source: 2022 Toolkit Annex I for complete item text and A1–C2 labels; official2023 report p.11/Annex1 for seventh not-aware option and0–6 point mapping. The2023 report omits the B2 row for6.5; no omitted row was invented.
These are self-reported digital-competence positions, not observed teaching, student learning outcomes, professional certification, personality labels or a school/teacher ranking.

The six separate digital area units, instructions, feedback and conservative missing policy are project adaptations. Current online text, independent-area validity and Chinese-version validity were not established.

Missing answers remain null and are not treated as a zero-point not-aware response. Any missing competence makes this area invalid/incomplete for interpretation. Other area units have their own completeness; no missing value is imputed. This project policy is not claimed as an author-issued missing-data algorithm.

No area average, global192-point score, overall proficiency band, population norm, percentile or cross-tool total is supplied. Consult the official Toolkit and2023 report for original glossary and full-tool interpretation.
report.disclaimer: For supportive professional learning reflection by the teacher receiving their own authorized results. A1–C2 are this framework’s maturity codes, not grades for teacher quality. No EU endorsement, badge or certificate is issued. Existing access and feedback permissions still apply.

instruction.text: Reflect on your current professional digital practice. For each competence choose the ONE statement that best describes your current position. A1, A2, B1, B2, C1 and C2 are progressive, item-specific statements; they are not agreement ratings. If appropriate, choose “I am not aware of this competence”, which is a real zero-point answer. A missing response remains missing. This digital unit is one area of the fixed2022 SELFIEforTEACHERS Toolkit and uses the official per-item0–6 mapping described in2023. Feedback is for your professional learning, not teacher appraisal, EU certification or student-outcome prediction.
instruction.source: Project-written digital instruction grounded in JRC129699 Toolkit self-reflection navigation/AnnexI and JRC131282 p.11/Annex1; not a verbatim official platform instruction.
